children: CoreWeave
led AI-related stocks into the red during a Friday free fall affecting much of the tech sector.

CoreWeave shares had declined nearly 12% by early afternoon trading. The AI data center company has plunged 34% over the past 10 days. The declines reflect a growing concern among investors that the AI infrastructure boom could become increasingly difficult to finance, particularly if inflation keeps interest rates elevated and customers struggle to generate sufficient returns on their investments.
Fellow neocloud, Nebius, shed 11%. Its share value has collapsed nearly 33% over the past 10 days. IREN
declined 10%. It has collapsed 34% since October 6, following the same downward spiral as CoreWeave and Nebius over that time frame.
Hardware providers were also feeling the pain on Friday, as evidenced by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index
sinking 2.8%. Micron
fell 4%, AMD
dropped 5%, and Intel
declined 4.9%. Nvidia
held on better, inching down 1%. Its share value has lost 10% since October 6.
Networking and optical shares were sinking as well. Lumentum
declined 4%, Coherent
dropped 6% and Celestica
slid 3.5%.
While financing and fears of inadequate future revenue generation are prompting much of the sell-offs, the AI infrastructure buildout appears to remain unabated. Evidence for this appeared in TSMC's
latest quarterly earnings
, which was released on Thursday.
Interestingly, analog and mixed-signal semiconductor stocks have remained more resilient. Texas Instruments
inched up 0.4% on Friday. Analog Devices
was relatively flat, and Onsemi
was down 1%. Although these have all declined since October 6, the drops have not been as pronounced.
Software was not exempt from Friday's bleeding. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF
had declined nearly 5% by afternoon trading.
A pullback in AI-related stocks has weighed on the broader market this week, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance. SK Hynix
fell 5.7% on Friday.

title: CoreWeave leads AI-related stocks lower during Friday free fall
